prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1483; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured states the other vehicle crossed into their lane on a curve at low speed. Both drivers reported no airbag deployment and both vehicles were driven from the scene. Initial liability appears disputed pending police report. Claimant reports back strain and has retained counsel, who has requested that all contact be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report received. Responding officer noted minor front-end damage to both vehicles and documented the other driver's statement that they were attempting to avoid debris. Preliminary fault assessment under review. Attorney's office confirmed representation in writing and asked for the claimant's medical authorization forms. Forms sent. Reserve set for bodily injury and property damage pending evaluation.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles reviewed. Damage consistent with reported low-speed impact. Repair estimate for insured vehicle obtained from shop of insured's choice. Independent appraiser assigned to other vehicle. Attorney's office has submitted a demand package listing treatment for lumbar strain, including chiropractic visits and a course of physical therapy. Records requested from listed providers and are being reviewed for prior history of back complaints.

Entry 4: Medical records received from primary care provider. Documentation notes onset of lower back pain the day after the collision with muscle spasm on exam, no neurological deficits, and no imaging ordered at this time. Prior visit from several years ago references intermittent back discomfort, which counsel has been asked to address. Desk review scheduled with the claims supervisor to evaluate causation and the reasonableness of the treatment plan. Communication with the attorney's office continues in writing only.

Entry 5: Supervisor review completed. Liability position updated to shared, pending the other carrier's response on comparative fault. Bodily injury evaluation is on hold until the physical therapy discharge summary is received. Attorney's office was advised in writing that the file remains open and that a settlement position will follow once the records are complete. Diary set for follow-up in thirty days.
